actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
Trim dead or rotted roots with clean scissors if found
Scratch-test stems to find living tissue
Cut vines back to last healthy green node and remove dead sections
Propagate node cuttings in water or moist sponge
Repot into slightly larger pot with drainage holes and fresh aroid mix
Remove from decorative cachepot or ensure water doesn't pool
Check top inch of soil is dry before watering again
Move plant to bright, indirect light away from drafts and hot sun
Train vines onto a moss pole, trellis, or hanging basket
Share plant name or close-up root photo for further advice

reason: The answer mainly blames rootbound and drought stress, noting the long, bare vines only as a symptom; it suggests cutting back only dead parts rather than the hard 60-80% trim that fixed the plant, and nothing it recommends is harmful.
